newsitem.title: CANADA: TrizecHahn shares gain in wake of issue.
newsitem.headline: TrizecHahn shares gain in wake of issue.

text.p: TrizecHahn Corp shares gained sharly for a second session on Wednesday in the wake of the company's announcement on Monday of a new issue of 12.5 million shares.
"I attribute the weakness and now the recovery to the recent share issue that was announced," said Frank Mayer, real estate analyst with HSBC James Capel Canada.

TrizecHahn shares rose C$1.05 to C$32.30 in midafternoon trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange. More than 27,000 shares had changed hands. On Monday following the announcement the stock closed at a two-month low of C$30.25.

"Many of the people who were buying the shares on the marketplace probably realized they could get a better deal by buying the issue and so that had initial negative effect," said Mayer. "Then people realized the infusion of this amount of cash would have a positive effect on the company, because it is achieving cash-on-cash returns in the range of 20 percent, and that the share price should be headed higher, not lower."

TrizecHahn's announcment yesterday that it will lease Toronto's landmark CN tower and build and retail and entertainment complex at the base was a positive for the stock, said Mayer. But he said the size of the share price rise was too large to be accounted for by a single deal.
"I don't think the announcement of a project here or a project there by itself can move capitalization to the magnitude it has," said Mayer.

The TrizecHahn CN Tower project is expected to cost at least C$100 million to develop, according to Jon Grant, chairman of Canada Lands Company Ltd, which currently owns the CN Tower property. A final agreement with TrizecHahn is expected within 30 days, he said.
